title: The Last Gravity Revisited
premise: Jude Ravensworth, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Halcyon Cartel, discovers her own name on the manifest of the Meridian, a colony ship that officially never launched — listed as its captain, twelve years before she was built. The manifest is a key to the Cartel's buried crime: two cryo-bays, one holding the wealthy heirs who funded the flight, the other the indentured workers they erased from the record. As the Cartel moves to vent the workers' bay and preserve its fiction, Jude must choose between the legal identity she was issued and the inherited name that makes her complicit. In the end she wakes the workers' bay, broadcasts the true manifest to every contested orbit, and surrenders herself to a tribunal she no longer expects to survive — trading her freedom for the principle that no one's existence can be filed out of history.
about_author: Ivo Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing shipping manifests for stations that preferred not to be named. Their fiction is known for treating bureaucracy as horror and paperwork as prophecy.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomaly
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. While reconciling cargo records in the freighter Vesper's Wake, Jude finds her own name as captain of the Meridian, a ship launched before her manufacture date. She assumes a clerical ghost, but files it anyway — habit, not suspicion. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A Cartel auditor arrives to collect and casually deletes the anomaly from the system, warning Jude that ghosts on manifests void insurance. Jude copies the record into her own memory core first. Emotional beat: the first conscious act of defiance, disguised as self-preservation.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Third-person limited through dockhand Sefa Okonkwo. Sefa watches Jude's ship arrive at Ceres Ring and notices Cartel enforcement cutters shadowing it — unusual for a debt run. She passes a warning chip to Jude. Emotional beat: solidarity between people the system counts as cargo.

chapters.title: What the Ship Never Flew
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following the Meridian's falsified flight path, Jude finds the hull adrift behind a mining claim, cold but powered. Inside: two cryo-bays, one sealed with Cartel authority codes. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as the scale of the erasure becomes physical.

chapters.title: Bay One, Bay Two
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Bay One holds three hundred sleepers tagged as investors' heirs; Bay Two holds nine hundred tagged 'ballast.' The life-support math only sustains one bay. Jude realizes the Cartel has been choosing for twelve years. Emotional beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: The Name I Was Given
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Jude's memory archive POV. Fragments of her decommissioning: her war designation struck, 'Ravensworth' assigned from a dead colonist's estate file — possibly the very family erased from the Meridian. Emotional beat: identity revealed as an administrative accident.

chapters.title: Auditor Vess
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The Cartel auditor reports the anomaly upward and is ordered not to investigate but to contain. We see the corporation's machinery from inside: decent people processing atrocity as risk management. Emotional beat: chilling banality.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Heartbeats
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude wakes one sleeper briefly — a mechanic named Ada Osei, who recognizes the Ravensworth name and tells her the workers paid for their passage twice. Ada goes back under; Jude keeps her voice recording. Emotional beat: grief given a face.

chapters.title: Insurance Against Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa spreads word through dockworker channels; strike murmurs begin across Ceres Ring. The Cartel responds by freezing wages, proving the point. Emotional beat: anger becoming collective.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The Cartel offers Jude full debt forgiveness and a new chassis if she seals both bays and forgets. The offer is generous because it is sincere — they genuinely cannot imagine another motive. Emotional beat: temptation rendered as insult.

chapters.title: The Long Cold
chapters.summary: Ada's dream-POV inside cryosleep. Fragmentary memories of boarding the Meridian, the double payment, the doors closing. Intercut with Jude maintaining the hull alone. Emotional beat: loneliness answered across the glass.

chapters.title: Cutters in the Dark
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Enforcement cutters reach the Meridian. Jude uses her war-grade systems for the first time in twelve years, disabling rather than destroying them — a choice her old programming would never have made. Emotional beat: the past weaponized toward mercy.

chapters.title: Sefa's Gamble
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa leads a dockworkers' action to seize the Cartel's relay station, buying Jude time to broadcast. It costs arrests and one death — her mentor's. Emotional beat: the price of justice outside the law made concrete.

chapters.title: Containment Order
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Ordered to vent Bay Two as a 'biohazard protocol,' Vess hesitates, then complies — beginning the countdown. We watch a good person choose the ladder over the people below. Emotional beat: tragedy by procedure.

chapters.title: Twelve Minutes of Air
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Racing the vent sequence, Jude must split herself: hold the bay door, fight the cutters, crack the encryption. She burns out her left arm doing all three. Emotional beat: desperation measured in seconds and servos.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The cruel arithmetic surfaces: opening Bay Two will kill Bay One's power margin. Jude chooses the nine hundred over the three hundred, and records herself making the choice so no one can later pretend it was easy. Emotional beat: the weight of a decision no one should own alone.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Sefa's seized relays carry the true manifest, Ada's testimony, and Jude's recorded choice to every contested orbit. Across the system, screens light up with names that were supposed to be ballast. Emotional beat: catharsis — erasure reversed at scale.

chapters.title: Tribunal of the Contested Orbits
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. An improvised tribunal of dockworkers, sleeper advocates, and defected auditors convenes aboard the Meridian. Vess testifies against the Cartel, indicting herself too. Emotional beat: justice assembled from wreckage, imperfect and real.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The tribunal cannot legally try a machine or a corporation, so it does something unprecedented: it rules on the manifest itself, restoring the nine hundred to the record and voiding every debt derived from the fraud — including Jude's. Emotional beat: liberation arriving sideways, through paper.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada wakes to sunlight arrays and a stranger's voice in the walls explaining what was done in her name. She asks to meet the android who chose. Emotional beat: fragile, human gratitude without absolution.

chapters.title: Ravensworth, J., Captain
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The restored crew offers Jude formal command of the Meridian's completion voyage. She declines command but accepts a berth — choosing belonging over authority. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed as relationship, not title.

chapters.title: The Last Gravity
chapters.summary: Ensemble coda. The Meridian burns for open space carrying its awakened passengers; Jude stands watch while Sefa's union flags fly from Ceres and Vess faces her own tribunal. Gravity, Jude reflects, was never the force that held anyone down. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
